correctness.rationale: The positive endpoint is exactly Calderoni--Yanowitz Theorem 1.1. Below the first weakly compact cardinal, Shelah--Struengmann's V=L construction provides an increasing continuous lambda-chain of free groups of size below lambda whose union G is indecomposable and has cardinality lambda. By Calderoni--Yanowitz Proposition 2.7 this chain makes G lambda-projective as a Z-module. G cannot be projective: over Z projective means free, and an uncountable free abelian group has a nontrivial basis partition and hence a direct-sum decomposition. Thus the universal small-ring property fails at every regular uncountable lambda below the first weakly compact cardinal.

value.rationale: This gives an exact sharpness theorem for the recent weakly compact projectivity result. It identifies a natural least-cardinal boundary among regular uncountable cardinals in L and shows every lower failure is witnessed over Z, so the obstruction is not an artifact of complicated rings. This is structural information about the precise large-cardinal strength of universal almost-projective compactness.
